notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Arizona county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Arizona yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Cochise County Sheriff's Office introduced a new drone program in fall 2025 for surveilling the U.S.-Mexico border. It has used drones since at least 2015.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003147, citing KJZZ

redFlags.label: Face recognition
redFlags.detail: The Cochise County Sheriff's Office spent $40,792 in June 2024 for Clearview AI face recognition technologyl.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS018295, citing Cochise County

redFlags.label: Cell-site simulator
redFlags.detail: While the Cochise County Sheriff’s Office does not own a cell-site simulator, search warrant records obtained by a local reporter show that deputies have the ability to access such a device maintained by the U.S. Marshals Service.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS000693, citing Bisbee Justice Court

redFlags.label: Video analytics
redFlags.detail: The Cochise County Sheriff's Office began using Cogniac software in 2018 to analyze footage from wilderness cameras placed along the U.S.-Mexico border.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS001956, citing Cochise County

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 2 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Douglas's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
